knowledge.markdown:
# Knowledge Base: Riemann Hypothesis

## The Problem

The Riemann Hypothesis (RH) is arguably the most famous unsolved problem in mathematics. Proposed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859, it concerns the distribution of prime numbers.

### Core Statement

> All non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function ζ(s) have real part equal to 1/2.

## What We Have Built

### RiemannHypothesis.lean (1531 lines, 90 declarations)

Comprehensive formalization including:
- Precise formal statement of RH using Mathlib riemannZeta
- 7 equivalent formulations: Robin, Lagarias, Mertens, Koch, Nyman-Beurling, de Bruijn-Newman, Weil
- Proved structural results: symmetry, quadruple symmetry, fundamental domain, non-real zeros
- Proved zeta values: ζ(2k) general formula, ζ(-k) formula, ζ(0)=-1/2
- GRH formalization with GRH⟹RH proved
- De Bruijn-Newman constant: 0 ≤ Λ ≤ 0.2 proved, RH ↔ Λ=0

### In Mathlib (Current)

| Component | Status |
|-----------|--------|
| Riemann zeta ζ(s) | ✅ Full (riemannZeta) |
| Functional equation | ✅ (riemannZeta_one_sub) |
| Euler product | ✅ (riemannZeta_eulerProduct_tprod) |
| Non-vanishing Re(s)≥1 | ✅ (PNT-strength) |
| Completed zeta Λ(s) | ✅ (completedRiemannZeta) |
| Dirichlet L-functions | ✅ (DirichletCharacter.LFunction) |
| Bernoulli numbers | ✅ |
| Harmonic numbers | ✅ |
| Analytic continuation | ✅ (built into riemannZeta) |

## Key References

- Lagarias (2002). An elementary problem equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis. AMM.
- Rodgers-Tao (2020). The de Bruijn-Newman constant is non-negative.
- Platt-Trudgian (2021). Λ ≤ 0.2.
